mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be negative due to persistent higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day horizon, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero-move baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during qualifying periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as labor market strength offsets inflationary pressure.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 5% month-over-month and CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.3% month-over-month in the same month
regime_hint: labor market strengthening with inflationary acceleration
failure_condition: During qualifying triggers, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat (mean return < 0.1%) with wide confidence intervals.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side resilience, leading to positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_12mo_mavg for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During qualifying supply shocks, SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (HOUST) decline by more than 3% in two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative as weak demand reduces corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by > 3% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (mean < -0.2%, p > 0.10) during qualifying episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% for a month followed by a decline below 3.8% predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as the labor market normalizes.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.0% and UNRATE < 3.8% in consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market adjustment after recessionary episode
failure_condition: During qualifying regime shifts, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both retail sales (HOUST) and consumer confidence (implied via labor indicators like PAYEMS) above their 12-month moving averages for two months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST_12mo_mavg AND PAYEMS > PAYEMS_12mo_mavg for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During qualifying interaction periods, SPX 20-day forward returns are flat or negative (mean ≤ 0.0%).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in industrial production (INDPRO) contraction—declines in two consecutive months followed by a rebound—yields a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as market interprets stabilization.
failure_condition: During double-dip episodes, SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months in a regime of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 4%), the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative due to market anticipation of wage-price spirals.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS > 4.0% in the same period
regime_hint: tightening cycle with labor market cooling
failure_condition: During qualifying regime, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (mean ≥ 0.05%, p > 0.05).
